question: What is the primary goal of community-wide vaccination programs?

options.A: To build herd immunity and protect vulnerable populations
options.B: To replace the need for handwashing and environmental sanitation
options.C: To cure individuals who are already experiencing severe symptoms
options.D: To completely eliminate all bacteria living inside the human gut

explanation: High immunization coverage creates a protective barrier of immune individuals, stopping the spread of disease to those who cannot be vaccinated. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T7#GNS313_U2_T7_h6)

question: What is the main reason special diets must respect a patient's culture?

options.A: To speed up the healing of surgical wounds
options.B: To ensure the patient actually eats the food provided
options.C: To reduce the cost of buying groceries
options.D: To prevent allergic reactions in the home

explanation: You got it! If a meal plan ignores a patient's cultural tastes, they simply won't eat it, leading to poor nutrition.

question: What is the internationally accepted age below which any marriage is classified as an early or child marriage?

options.A: Under 18 years of age
options.B: Under 15 years of age
options.C: Under 16 years of age
options.D: Under 21 years of age

explanation: Great job! Global health standards consider anyone under 18 a minor. Any union below this age is classed as early marriage, no matter local customs.

question: Where do bedside nurses usually spot their first research ideas?

options.A: By reading financial audits of hospital pharmacies
options.B: Through political debates in national assemblies
options.C: Inside historical textbooks written decades ago
options.D: During routine patient care observations and shift routines

explanation: As nurses, we see what happens on the ward every single day. Your daily clinical experiences are a goldmine for research topics!

question: As a bedside nurse, why are you considered right at the center of hospital waste management?

options.A: Nurses are the only staff members allowed to touch trash
options.B: Nurses are legally liable for the city waste trucks
options.C: Nurses generate waste during daily patient care activities
options.D: Hospital management forces nurses to pay for disposal bins

explanation: Spot on! Because we give direct patient care every day, we are the first ones to handle and discard medical materials.

question: What makes an abortion procedure classified as "unsafe"?

options.A: An elective termination performed using modern pharmaceutical drugs
options.B: Any pregnancy loss occurring naturally during the first trimester
options.C: A legal surgical procedure performed by a certified gynecologist
options.D: A termination done without proper medical training or in unsterile settings

explanation: You've got this! An unsafe abortion simply means it was carried out by untrained hands or in dirty places, which puts the patient at a huge risk for severe complications. Spotting this definition helps you protect your patients early!

question: Why are schools considered great spots for public health interventions?

options.A: Schools have unlimited financial resources to buy medical equipment
options.B: Teachers possess advanced clinical degrees in nursing and medicine
options.C: Students are legally required to receive medical treatment at school
options.D: Children spend a large portion of their formative years gathered in one place

explanation: Spot on! When children are gathered in one learning spot, public health workers can easily reach many of them at once to build healthy habits.

question: Which vaccine is routinely administered to pregnant women during antenatal care visits to prevent a specific neonatal infection?

options.A: Tetanus toxoid
options.B: Measles vaccine
options.C: Oral polio vaccine
options.D: Bacille Calmette-Guérin

explanation: Pregnant women receive tetanus toxoid injections during antenatal visits to protect both mother and newborn against tetanus. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T7#GNS124_U2_T7_h4)

question: Which of the following is a modifiable cardiovascular risk factor?

options.A: Biological sex at birth
options.B: Family history of heart disease
options.C: Elevated blood pressure
options.D: Advanced chronological age

explanation: Blood pressure can be modified through diet, exercise, and medication, whereas age, sex, and genetics cannot be changed. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T15#GNS213_U1_T15_h2)

question: Which meningeal layer wraps around the brain so tightly that it dips into every single groove and fold?

options.A: Dura mater
options.B: Arachnoid mater
options.C: Periosteal layer
options.D: Pia mater

explanation: You got it! The pia mater is soft and tender, clinging closely to every curve of the brain like a second skin.

question: Which lifestyle habit directly helps improve pelvic blood circulation and mood?

options.A: Eating high-fat processed foods
options.B: Avoiding physical activity
options.C: Regular aerobic exercise
options.D: Smoking cigarettes daily

explanation: Aerobic exercise strengthens the cardiovascular system, improves blood flow throughout the body, and releases feel-good endorphins. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T26#GNS312_U1_T26_h6)

question: Which area in the TSSU uses negative air pressure?

options.A: Preparation zone
options.B: Decontamination zone
options.C: Sterile storage zone
options.D: Packaging zone

explanation: Spot on! The dirty (decontamination) zone has negative air pressure so that air flows inward, trapping germs and stopping them from floating out into cleaner rooms.

question: After a very tough loss on the children's ward, what best helps the nursing team cope with the stress?

options.A: Forcing the team to take on extra admissions to stay busy
options.B: Pretending the event did not happen to maintain normal routines
options.C: Punishing the nurses immediately for failing to save the patient
options.D: Providing a safe space for structured team debriefing and counseling

explanation: Talking through grief together in a supportive session helps nurses heal and prevents long-term emotional burnout.

question: In a strongly patriarchal setting, who usually makes the final decision on family size?

options.A: The junior nursing officer
options.B: The male head of the household
options.C: The youngest child in the family
options.D: The local government chairman

explanation: Correct! In these settings, men or senior family members traditionally call the shots on major household matters like family size.

question: What is the primary reason for initiating a patient referral to another facility?

options.A: The hospital building needs routine plumbing repairs
options.B: The patient's clinical needs exceed current facility resources
options.C: The attending doctor wants to take a short vacation
options.D: The patient complains about the food quality on the ward

explanation: Referrals are done when specialized care, advanced equipment, or specific expertise is required that the current health center cannot provide. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h4)

question: What does the politics of health services primarily study?

options.A: How to diagnose infectious tropical diseases
options.B: The chemical formulas of essential drugs
options.C: How power and money shape healthcare delivery
options.D: The daily cleaning routines in hospital wards

explanation: This field examines how authority, funding, and policy decisions control access to medical care and resource distribution. [learn more](GST321_U6_T3#GST321_U6_T3_h1)

question: Which of the following is an appropriate nursing action when supporting a family undergoing genetic counseling?

options.A: Telling the family which genetic diagnosis they should accept
options.B: Making the final decision on whether the couple should have children
options.C: Ordering complex chromosomal laboratory tests independently
options.D: Reinforcing educational information and providing emotional support

explanation: Nurses support patients by reinforcing explanations given by genetic specialists and offering a compassionate listening ear, while respecting patient autonomy. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T7#GNS111_U1_T7_h7)

question: What is the classic sign that a patient has entered the prodromal stage of an infection?

options.A: Vague feelings of tiredness and mild body discomfort
options.B: Sudden appearance of distinct, textbook skin rashes
options.C: Full-blown paralysis of the lower extremities
options.D: Complete recovery of normal daily energy levels

explanation: That's it! The prodromal stage is when the patient just feels 'off' or unusually tired before the main symptoms show up.

question: What is the main purpose of using the Z-track technique during an IM injection?

options.A: To push the needle deeper into the major blood vessels
options.B: To stretch the skin so the needle insertion causes no pain
options.C: To make it easier to aspirate blood before injecting
options.D: To seal the medication inside the muscle and prevent skin staining

explanation: Pulling the skin sideways before insertion offsets the tissue layers, sealing the track so irritating drugs cannot leak upward. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T6#GNS125_U3_T6_h4)

question: Where should the patient stand on the platform during a weight measurement?

options.A: Leaning against the wall for proper balance
options.B: As far forward as possible to see the numbers
options.C: In the exact center with weight distributed evenly
options.D: With one foot on the floor for stability

explanation: Standing centrally with balanced footing ensures the entire body mass rests squarely on the weighing mechanism. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T8#GNS225_U2_T8_h5)

question: What does 'cultural humility' mean for a home health nurse?

options.A: Recognizing personal biases and respecting the patient's cultural beliefs
options.B: Ignoring cultural differences to treat everyone identically
options.C: Reading a textbook about a culture before every visit
options.D: Convincing the patient to adopt the nurse's personal lifestyle

explanation: It's all about checking your own biases at the door and keeping an open mind about how a patient's background shapes their health choices.

question: Which contraceptive option is a long-acting reversible method placed right inside the uterus?

options.A: Combined oral pill
options.B: Emergency contraceptive pill
options.C: Spermicidal foam
options.D: Intrauterine device

explanation: An IUD is a fantastic, worry-free option that sits quietly inside the uterus for years, providing continuous protection that you can stop anytime.

question: When does the immediate puerperium period happen?

options.A: Between the second and sixth week
options.B: Before the placenta is delivered
options.C: The first 24 hours after delivery
options.D: The entire first week after birth

explanation: Spot on! The immediate puerperium covers the first 24 hours post-delivery. As nurses, we watch new mums closely during this window because the risk for heavy bleeding is at its highest.

question: Why do cancer drugs (cytotoxic drugs) cause hair loss and upset stomachs?

options.A: The drugs accumulate exclusively in the skin
options.B: Healthy cells actively absorb the toxins
options.C: These healthy tissues also divide rapidly
options.D: The immune system attacks the medicine

explanation: Great thinking! Because these drugs target fast division, they accidentally affect normal body parts that also grow quickly, like hair roots and stomach lining.

question: What is the main difference between a pathogen's 'reservoir' and its 'source'?

options.A: A reservoir is found inside the human body, while a source is always environmental
options.B: There is no difference between the two terms in clinical epidemiology
options.C: A reservoir only contains viruses, while a source only transmits bacterial infections
options.D: A reservoir is the natural habitat of a pathogen, while a source is the immediate point of transmission

explanation: A reservoir is where the germ lives comfortably and multiplies (like its home), whereas the source is the exact thing that hands it over to you.

question: A nurse checks clinic attendance registers to see which illnesses bring patients in most often. What is this called?

options.A: Reviewing epidemiological data
options.B: Performing environmental observation
options.C: Conducting cultural mapping
options.D: Establishing peer pressure groups

explanation: Spot on! Looking at clinic records to track disease patterns is a classic way we gather epidemiological data to plan our next steps.

question: Which scenario is an example of natural passive immunity?

options.A: A patient recovering completely from a severe bout of malaria
options.B: A pregnant woman receiving a tetanus toxoid booster shot
options.C: An infant receiving protective antibodies through breast milk
options.D: A traveler receiving a shot of hepatitis B immunoglobulin

explanation: Passing antibodies from a mother to her baby via breast milk or the placenta is a natural way to provide temporary passive protection. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T8#GNS313_U1_T8_h4)

question: Why is advance notice of duty rosters important for nursing staff?

options.A: It stops patients from complaining about the food
options.B: It helps nurses plan their personal lives and reduces fatigue
options.C: It allows the hospital to buy drugs at cheaper wholesale prices
options.D: It removes the need for any night shifts on the ward

explanation: Predictable schedules allow staff to rest properly and manage family responsibilities, lowering burnout. [learn more](GST321_U1_T11#GST321_U1_T11_h5)

question: How do most drugs cross cell membranes when they are being absorbed?

options.A: Pinocytosis
options.B: Osmotic pressure
options.C: Passive diffusion
options.D: Active transport

explanation: Most drugs just cruise right through cell membranes via passive diffusion—moving smoothly from an area of high concentration to low concentration without using up any energy!

question: What is the main reason we preserve food?

options.A: To completely eliminate all vitamins from food items
options.B: To replace natural food colors with artificial dyes
options.C: To stop or slow down food spoilage and microbial growth
options.D: To make food taste significantly sweeter and saltier

explanation: Food preservation stops germs and chemical reactions from spoiling our meals, helping keep food safe to eat later!

question: Why must a waiting patient be reassessed periodically in the emergency department?

options.A: Nurses need to practice their physical assessment skills
options.B: Their clinical condition can deteriorate over time
options.C: Hospital policy mandates a chat every ten minutes
options.D: It prevents patients from leaving without paying

explanation: A patient categorized as stable during initial triage can suddenly worsen, making ongoing reassessment a critical safety measure. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T1#GNS315_U1_T1_h3)

question: What is the standard laboratory test used to confirm an intestinal Ascaris infection?

options.A: Complete blood count with differential
options.B: Liver function blood test panel
options.C: Stool microscopy for ova and parasites
options.D: Chest X-ray imaging for lung infiltrates

explanation: Checking a stool sample under a microscope for roundworm eggs is the easiest and most reliable way to confirm the diagnosis.

question: Which of these is a major warning sign of fake nutrition advice?

options.A: Advising patients to eat a balanced variety of all food groups
options.B: Publishing raw data from randomized and controlled clinical trials
options.C: Requiring regular blood tests supervised by a registered dietitian
options.D: Promising a single product can cure many different diseases

explanation: If one simple tea or supplement claims to cure everything from malaria to headaches, run the other way! Real medicine doesn't work that way.

question: What is the main goal of palliative care when dealing with advanced breast cancer?

options.A: To train the patient to perform clinical breast exams on others
options.B: To reverse the side effects of prior chemotherapy drugs
options.C: To improve quality of life and relieve distressing symptoms
options.D: To completely cure the metastatic cancer cells in the bones

explanation: When a cure isn't possible anymore, palliative care steps in to wrap the patient in comfort, pain relief, and dignity.

question: A patient proudly tells you they stopped eating all carbs and dairy to lose weight fast. What is your next best step as a nurse?

options.A: Immediately prescribe a high-calorie hospital diet to reverse the weight loss
options.B: Congratulate the patient on achieving rapid weight loss without any concern
options.C: Assess for nutrient deficiencies and discuss the health risks of restrictive eating
options.D: Tell the patient to stop visiting the clinic until they reach their target goal

explanation: Always educate gently! Check their nutritional health and calmly explain why cutting out entire food groups can hurt them in the long run.

question: Which laboratory test is used to definitively diagnose sickle cell anaemia?

options.A: Erythrocyte sedimentation rate
options.B: Coagulation profile test
options.C: Complete blood count
options.D: Haemoglobin electrophoresis

explanation: Haemoglobin electrophoresis is the gold standard test! It separates different types of haemoglobin in a sample so the lab can clearly spot abnormal haemoglobin S.

question: What is a common myth that stops people from using family planning in many communities?

options.A: Family planning guarantees you will have a baby boy
options.B: Contraceptives are made only by local farmers
options.C: Using a condom cures all infections instantly
options.D: Modern contraceptives cause permanent infertility

explanation: You nailed it! A lot of people fear that using birth control now means they won't be able to bear children later, which isn't true.

question: What makes evacuating a sick patient off a ship so tricky and dangerous?

options.A: Excessive paperwork required by land-based police
options.B: The legal prohibition of helicopters over international waters
options.C: Adverse weather and difficult transfer conditions at sea
options.D: Lack of any communication tools between ship and shore

explanation: Spot on! Shifting waves and high winds make moving a patient via helicopter hoist or between two moving boats extremely risky.

question: What is the main ethical focus of nursing care during the final stages of a degenerative disease?

options.A: Preserving patient dignity and providing comfort
options.B: Limiting family visits to reduce hospital noise and confusion
options.C: Forcing the patient to eat regular meals against their will
options.D: Finding experimental genetic treatments to reverse brain damage

explanation: You nailed it! When a disease reaches its end stage, the goal shifts from stopping the decline to ensuring comfort, pain relief, and deep dignity. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T13#GNS222_U4_T13_h7)

question: Why do red blood cells change into a sickle shape in this condition?

options.A: The bone marrow produces cells with too much iron and water inside them
options.B: Haemoglobin S molecules stick together to form rigid rods when they release oxygen
options.C: White blood cells attack and deform the healthy red blood cells
options.D: Excess sugar in the bloodstream causes the red blood cells to shrink and warp

explanation: When haemoglobin S delivers oxygen to body tissues, it clumps into stiff strands that distort the normal round cell into a crescent shape. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h1)

question: What is the proper term for professional negligence committed by a healthcare provider?

options.A: Insubordination
options.B: Defamation
options.C: Battery
options.D: Malpractice

explanation: Malpractice simply means professional negligence—when a healthcare provider fails to meet the expected standard of care and a patient gets hurt. You will master these terms easily!

question: What is the primary characteristic of a generic drug name?

options.A: It is exclusively owned and trademarked by one manufacturing company
options.B: It is the official non-proprietary name for the active ingredient
options.C: It changes depending on which country the medication is imported from
options.D: It describes the exact atomic arrangement of the chemical structure

explanation: The generic name is the universal, public name given to the active drug, no matter who manufactures it. Think of it as the drug's true identity!

question: Why is accurate timing and documentation following a cardiac arrest event so crucial?

options.A: It replaces the need for a verbal handover to the intensive care unit
options.B: It guarantees insurance payment for hospital equipment used
options.C: It is required only if the resuscitation attempt was completely successful
options.D: It provides a clear legal and clinical record of the emergency timeline

explanation: Detailed notes record the exact interventions and timing, which helps evaluate patient outcomes and guide future care. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T1#GNS212_U2_T1_h8)

question: How does the Methylene Blue Reductase Test estimate how many bacteria are in milk?

options.A: By detecting chemical toxins released by dying bacterial cells in the liquid
options.B: By measuring how fast bacteria use up oxygen and change the dye's color
options.C: By counting the visible colonies growing on a Petri dish after 24 hours
options.D: By measuring the drop in pH caused by acid-producing organisms

explanation: Spot on! Active bacteria eat up the dissolved oxygen in the milk, which makes the added blue dye lose its color faster. More bacteria means quicker color change!

question: Which part of the brain acts as the emotional alarm system that triggers the fight-or-flight response during anxiety?

options.A: The pituitary gland
options.B: The cerebellum
options.C: The medulla oblongata
options.D: The amygdala

explanation: Spot on! The amygdala is our emotional radar. It processes threats and sounds the alarm early when we feel anxious. You've got this!

question: What is the main difference between recruitment and selection?

options.A: Recruitment finds candidates, while selection chooses the best fit
options.B: Recruitment checks licenses, while selection checks exam scores
options.C: Selection is done by human resources, and recruitment is done by doctors
options.D: There is no difference between the two terms

explanation: Recruitment brings people in to apply, and selection is the screening process used to pick the right hire. [learn more](GST321_U1_T11#GST321_U1_T11_h3)

question: What is a major reason doctors prescribe corticosteroids for lung conditions?

options.A: To thin thick mucus so coughing is easier
options.B: To reduce airway swelling during severe asthma attacks
options.C: To kill bacterial germs inside the lungs
options.D: To lower high blood pressure in lung vessels

explanation: Well done! Steroids are powerful anti-inflammatory drugs that quickly open up swollen airways when an asthma attack strikes.

question: What does the intraperitoneal (IP) route actually mean?

options.A: Infusing fluids directly into a large peripheral vein
options.B: Swallowing drugs that dissolve in the stomach lining
options.C: Placing medicated patches onto the abdominal skin
options.D: Injecting medication directly into the peritoneal cavity

explanation: Great job! The intraperitoneal route simply means putting medication straight into the peritoneal cavity that surrounds your belly organs. Think of it as a direct shortcut to the abdominal space! [learn more](GNS125_U3_T11#GNS125_U3_T11_h1)

question: What is the main risk of delaying contraceptive counseling until the first post-procedure menstrual period?

options.A: An increased risk of an unintended repeat pregnancy
options.B: Immediate surgical complications from the abortion
options.C: Total loss of hormonal control in the body
options.D: Permanent damage to the ovarian lining

explanation: Because ovulation happens before the first period, waiting until menstruation returns leaves the client unprotected during the fertile window. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h1)

question: A patient with a history of severe blood clots asks for birth control after an abortion. Which method should you avoid?

options.A: Progestin-only injections
options.B: Copper intrauterine devices
options.C: Combined oral contraceptive pills
options.D: Male and female barrier condoms

explanation: Combined pills contain estrogen, which increases the risk of dangerous blood clots in patients who are already vulnerable to them.

question: What happens to the thymus gland as a person grows older?

options.A: It accumulates calcified deposits known as corpora arenacea
options.B: Its pinealocytes transform entirely into hormone-secreting neurons
options.C: It develops hollow colloid-filled follicles similar to the thyroid
options.D: It undergoes fatty involution and gradually shrinks in size

explanation: As we age, the active immune tissue in the thymus slowly gets replaced by fat cells—a natural process called involution. Nothing to worry about, it's just part of normal aging!

question: How is the daily amount of protein on a restricted diet typically calculated?

options.A: Percentage of total daily fluid intake
options.B: Cups per gallon of water consumed
options.C: Ounces per meal regardless of size
options.D: Grams per kilogram of body weight

explanation: Dietary protein prescriptions are personalized to the patient's body mass to ensure they receive enough for basic needs without overloading their organs. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T004#GNS227_U6_T004_h3)

question: What is the main goal of Mass Drug Administration (MDA) programs in communities with high worm rates?

options.A: Reducing the overall parasite burden across the entire population
options.B: Eliminating the need for basic sanitation and clean water supply
options.C: Curating permanent immunity against all bacterial and viral pathogens
options.D: Diagnosing individual complex surgical emergencies in local hospitals

explanation: MDA treats whole communities at once to quickly bring down the total number of worms and stop heavy transmission without needing individual lab tests.

question: Why is it important to separate a medical error from an unavoidable adverse event?

options.A: Adverse events always lead to immediate legal action against the nurse
options.B: Medical errors only happen in surgical wards, while adverse events happen in clinics
options.C: Unavoidable adverse events are always caused by nurse negligence
options.D: Errors involve preventable mistakes, while some adverse events are known risks of treatment

explanation: Recognizing the difference helps teams identify what could have been prevented versus what was an unpredictable reaction to care. [learn more](GST319_U6_T1#GST319_U6_T1_h1)

question: In nursing tests and exams, what does 'validity' actually mean?

options.A: The test can be completed in under twenty minutes.
options.B: Multiple instructors will always give the exact same grade.
options.C: The test gives the exact same score every single time it is used.
options.D: The test actually measures what it is intended to measure.

explanation: A valid test is one that truly assesses the exact skill or knowledge it claims to test. No tricks—just straight to the point!

question: What weather condition in tropical regions like Nigeria contributes greatly to skin fungal infections?

options.A: Frequent consumption of contaminated municipal water supplies
options.B: High environmental humidity and warm weather conditions
options.C: Lack of personal hygiene products in local markets
options.D: Widespread resistance to standard antibacterial vaccines

explanation: You got it! Fungi love warmth and moisture. Our wonderful tropical climate means we see plenty of superficial skin fungal infections in clinical practice.

question: Why should you NEVER use a patient's room number to verify who they are?

options.A: Doctors change room assignments every single hour
options.B: Room numbers are often painted the same color
options.C: Patients frequently switch rooms or beds
options.D: Hospital charts do not display room numbers

explanation: Beds and rooms change all the time in a busy ward. Location is never a safe way to identify a patient!

question: Why is emotional support and clear teaching so important for patients undergoing tests for blood disorders?

options.A: Kind words replace the need for local numbing medicine
options.B: Patients must memorize all lab ranges before going home
options.C: Clear explanations keep the lab machines from breaking down
options.D: The tests often look for serious illnesses like cancer, which causes high worry

explanation: Waiting for results on serious conditions can be terrifying. Your gentle reassurance and clear explanations make a world of difference for a worried patient.

question: Why must an effective screening program have accessible treatment available?

options.A: Treatment reduces the cost of running the laboratory
options.B: Patients will refuse to take the test otherwise
options.C: It proves the screening test is completely infallible
options.D: Finding a disease is useless if patients cannot get care

explanation: Screening only improves health outcomes if positive results lead to timely, effective medical interventions. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T4#GNS225_U2_T4_h3)

question: A nurse wants to screen an older adult for depression. Which tool should she use?

options.A: Geriatric Depression Scale
options.B: Braden Scale for Pressure Sores
options.C: Mini-Mental State Examination
options.D: Morse Fall Scale

explanation: The Geriatric Depression Scale is specifically made for older adults to check in on their mood. It's a quick and helpful screening tool in clinical practice.

question: Which long-term health risk is strongly linked to low oestrogen levels when amenorrhoea is left untreated?

options.A: Chronic kidney failure
options.B: Obstructive sleep apnea
options.C: Type 1 diabetes mellitus
options.D: Osteoporosis

explanation: Oestrogen helps keep bones strong and dense. When levels stay low for too long, bones can become weak and brittle over time.

question: How does chronic viral hepatitis usually behave differently from acute hepatitis in the early stages?

options.A: Chronic infections often cause no symptoms for many years while silently damaging the liver
options.B: Chronic infections always start with a sudden, violent fever and severe vomiting
options.C: Chronic infections resolve completely within two to four weeks without any treatment
options.D: Chronic infections only affect older adults with pre-existing kidney disease

explanation: That's why chronic strains like Hepatitis B and C can be so tricky—they can hide out in the body for years without giving any warning signs!

question: How often does a client usually change a transdermal contraceptive patch?

options.A: Once a month
options.B: Every six months
options.C: Every single day
options.D: Once a week

explanation: Think weekly! You apply a fresh patch once a week for three weeks straight, followed by one patch-free week.

question: What is the main job of your nasal cavity when you breathe in air?

options.A: To store excess air during heavy exercise
options.B: To produce sound waves for vocalization
options.C: To exchange oxygen directly into the bloodstream
options.D: To warm, humidify, and filter incoming air

explanation: Spot on! Your nose acts like a natural air conditioner, warming, cleaning, and moistening the air before it travels down into your lungs.

question: Which food item is a well-known high choking hazard for toddlers?

options.A: Soft bananas
options.B: Whole grapes
options.C: Mashed potatoes
options.D: Cooked oatmeal

explanation: Round, firm foods like whole grapes can easily block a child's small airway and must be cut into small pieces. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T4#GNS324_U6_T4_h6)

question: Why do newborn babies routinely get a vitamin K injection shortly after birth?

options.A: To reverse potential clotting factor loss from traumatic delivery
options.B: To stimulate immediate production of white blood cells
options.C: To prevent the development of inherited haemophilia
options.D: To make up for a sterile gut that cannot yet synthesize vitamin K

explanation: Babies are born with clean, sterile tummies that haven't grown the helpful gut bacteria needed to make vitamin K yet. That quick injection protects them from bleeding problems!

question: What happens to calcium levels inside smooth muscle cells when they need to relax?

options.A: Levels fluctuate in a rapid cycle
options.B: Levels decrease
options.C: Levels remain completely unchanged
options.D: Levels increase significantly

explanation: Good job! A drop in calcium stops the muscle fibers from sliding together, allowing the muscle to relax and widen.

question: How should a patient properly store their sublingual nitroglycerin tablets so they don't lose their strength?

options.A: Uncapped on the kitchen counter for easy access
options.B: In a clear plastic bag kept inside a warm pocket
options.C: Inside the bathroom medicine cabinet near the shower
options.D: In a dark, airtight glass container away from heat

explanation: Nitroglycerin is sensitive! Heat, light, and moisture destroy it quickly, which is why it stays safe in its original dark glass bottle.

question: A patient getting ready for discharge is worried about taking her pain pills right. What should you do first?

options.A: Tell the patient not to worry because pain is all in the mind
options.B: Cancel the prescription and give only herbal remedies instead
options.C: Ask a family member to manage all medication doses at home
options.D: Review the medication schedule slowly and check for understanding

explanation: Taking a little extra time to walk through the dosing schedule ensures the patient feels confident and safe at home. Excellent patient advocacy!

question: What is a fomite?

options.A: An inanimate object that can carry and transfer infectious germs
options.B: A living insect that transmits a parasite from animal to human
options.C: A specialized white blood cell that attacks invading bacteria
options.D: A type of protective mask worn during surgical procedures

explanation: Fomites are non-living items like door knobs, medical charts, and instruments that hold onto pathogens and pass them to new hosts. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T6#GNS313_U1_T6_h4)

question: Which factor most frequently disrupts healthy eating habits during adolescence?

options.A: An inability to digest complex carbohydrates
options.B: Peer pressure and preoccupation with body image
options.C: A natural biological loss of interest in eating
options.D: The complete disappearance of hunger cues

question: What is a major, life-threatening danger of an intracardiac injection?

question: What is the main difference between clinical fatigue and normal tiredness?

options.A: Clinical fatigue only affects muscle tissue, never the brain.
options.B: Normal tiredness lasts for several weeks without interruption.
options.C: Normal tiredness is caused exclusively by electrolyte imbalances.

question: Why do pregnant women and young children get severe malaria so easily in Nigeria?

question: A family caregiver caring for an advanced cancer patient at home appears exhausted, irritable, and states they have not slept through the night in weeks. What is the most appropriate nursing action?

options.A: Discuss options for respite care to give the caregiver a temporary break
options.B: Tell the caregiver that exhaustion is simply part of the job
options.C: Arrange for emergency placement of the patient in a permanent nursing home
options.D: Advise the caregiver to stop giving pain medications at night

question: Which method of giving a medication skips the absorption process completely?

options.A: Intravenous injection
options.B: Oral tablet ingestion

options.D: Subcutaneous injection

question: Why do non-experimental studies often have high ecological validity?

question: When we talk about 'food availability' in healthcare and nutrition, what does it mainly mean?

options.A: The physical presence of food in a specific area

question: Which leadership style is best when a sudden cholera outbreak needs immediate, fast action?

options.A: Autocratic

options.D: Democratic

question: What clinical advantage does seeing a patient at home give a nurse?

options.A: A chance to test all household appliances for electrical safety

question: Why must clean utility rooms be kept strictly separate from dirty utility spaces in a hospital?

options.A: To comply with financial auditing standards for medical supplies

options.C: To ensure that nurses can easily find their personal meal breaks

question: What is a major challenge many healthcare facilities in Nigeria face when trying to dispose of waste?

options.D: Lack of any medical waste being generated in wards

question: Why is it so helpful for a nurse to explain health concepts in local languages?

options.A: It replaces the need for clinical diagnosis

options.C: It speeds up the process of writing patient case notes
options.D: It helps patients understand and apply health practices

question: Why is fat stored around the abdomen (apple shape) more risky for health than fat on the hips (gynoid shape)?

question: What effect does staying in school usually have on a young girl's future marriage and childbirth?

options.A: It has no measurable impact on family planning or marriage timelines

question: Why are antiplatelet drugs like aspirin given to patients with peripheral artery disease?

question: What makes a nursing care plan truly 'individualized' in holistic practice?

options.C: Using the exact same printed template for every patient with malaria

question: Which quality of a study means that if you repeat it, you will get consistent results?

question: Why might a patient having a severe gout flare still show a completely normal blood uric acid level on a lab test?

question: Which of the following is NOT a common challenge faced by nurses providing community care for special children in Nigeria?

options.A: Excessive availability of well-funded pediatric specialists in rural clinics

question: Which part of the eye is damaged in all types of glaucoma?

options.A: The outer cornea
options.B: The crystalline lens

options.D: The white of the eye

question: Why do low-income communities often suffer more deaths during natural disasters?

options.A: Natural hazards target developing countries more frequently

question: What is the standard defaulter rate commonly measured in routine immunization programs?

question: Why is effective nutrition counselling more than just handing a patient a printed diet sheet?

question: What is the primary function of the large intestine during digestion?

options.A: Producing digestive enzymes for proteins
options.B: Absorbing water and salts from waste

options.D: Breaking down fats into fatty acids

question: A family member asks how to wash bed sheets stained with wound drainage. What should you tell them?

question: A nurse assesses a wound and notes it as 'mild, moderate, or severe'. What scale of measurement is this?

question: How can healthcare teams best build resilience in the face of infrastructural challenges?

question: Which of the following is NOT a core responsibility of a community health nurse in immunization programs?

question: Which group of vitamins needs dietary fat to be properly absorbed by your gut?

question: Why should nurses care about the mental health of patients with visible skin problems?

question: What vital sign must a nurse always check before administering certain heart medications like digoxin?

question: Why do certain cultural practices place strict food bans on women during pregnancy?

question: What happens immediately to your body when stress hormones like adrenaline rush into your bloodstream?

question: You walk into a stuffy ward, fling the windows open to let in fresh air, and tidy up a messy bedside. Whose classic nursing theory are you putting into action?

question: What was the main problem in drug markets before the WHO introduced essential drug guidelines?

question: How should a nurse manager guide a brand-new student nurse doing a complex procedure for the very first time?

question: What is a key nursing action to prevent bedsores (pressure injuries) in a resident who stays in bed all day?

question: What is the main job of proprioceptors during physical activity?

options.A: Speeding up blood flow inside bones
options.B: Releasing lubricating fluid into joints
options.C: Producing energy for resting muscles
options.D: Telling the brain about body position and muscle tension

explanation: Proprioceptors are your body's internal GPS! They constantly whisper to your brain about where your arms and legs are without you even having to look.

question: Which common health condition is a major cause of sudden breathlessness in Nigerian hospital wards?

options.A: Severe anaemia
options.B: Hemophilia A
options.C: Polycythaemia vera
options.D: Thrombocytopenia

explanation: Great job! Severe anaemia—often linked to malaria or poor nutrition—means fewer red blood cells to carry oxygen, making the patient breathe faster to compensate.

question: Which hormone keeps the uterus relaxed throughout pregnancy to prevent early labor?

options.A: progesterone
options.B: estrogen
options.C: oxytocin
options.D: prolactin

explanation: You got it! Progesterone is the main pregnancy-maintaining hormone that keeps the uterine muscles calm until it is time for delivery.

question: A 16-year-old girl visits the clinic showing signs of severe mood swings and sudden weight loss. What should you, as the nurse, suspect first?

options.A: Emerging psychosocial or mental health challenges typical of this age group
options.B: Normal age-related cognitive decline
options.C: Permanent physical disability from birth
options.D: Early onset geriatric syndrome

explanation: Well done! Teens experiencing emotional stress often show it through sudden changes in behavior, body image concerns, or physical symptoms. Always keep an eye out for their mental wellbeing.

question: How does standard phototherapy help lower bilirubin levels in a newborn?

options.A: It cools down the infant's skin to slow down the circulation of blood
options.B: It destroys red blood cells so they stop producing extra waste pigments
options.C: It stimulates the kidneys to produce concentrated, dark-colored urine
options.D: It changes bilirubin into water-soluble forms that the body can excrete easily

explanation: Special lights alter the bilirubin right in the skin, turning it into a form the baby can easily pass out without needing the liver to process it first. Science in action!

question: At what heart rate should you start chest compressions during newborn resuscitation?

options.A: Below 60 beats per minute
options.B: Below 80 beats per minute
options.C: Below 40 beats per minute
options.D: Below 100 beats per minute

explanation: If the heart rate drops below 60 despite good assisted breathing, the heart needs direct chest compressions to keep blood flowing.

question: Why must nurses be extra careful when giving psychiatric drugs to patients with brain degeneration?

options.A: These drugs completely stop the physical progression of the genetic disease
options.B: Medications only work if they are given through an intravenous line
options.C: Their damaged brains make them more sensitive to side effects like excessive sedation
options.D: Patients with degenerative conditions are immune to all forms of chemical treatment

explanation: Brilliant. Because the central nervous system is altered, even small doses can cause strong side effects like heavy sleepiness. Always start low and go slow! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T13#GNS222_U4_T13_h5)

question: A patient with large fibroids complains of constant tiredness, pale skin, and dizziness during her heavy periods. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Hormonal imbalance stopping ovulation completely
options.B: A sudden severe pelvic infection
options.C: Iron-deficiency anemia from chronic blood loss
options.D: Complete blockage of the cervix by scar tissue

explanation: Spot on! Losing a lot of blood month after month depletes the body's iron stores, leading to classic anemia symptoms like fatigue and paleness.

question: How does teaching a new family during postnatal home visits help them?

options.A: It replaces the need for any future childhood immunizations
options.B: It eliminates all expenses related to infant nutrition
options.C: It teaches them how to spot danger signs early in mother and baby
options.D: It guarantees that the baby will never catch common colds

explanation: When parents know what warning signs to look out for, they can report problems early and get quick medical help.

question: A patient asks why their salt intake matters so much for their blood pressure. What is your best response?

options.A: Salt stops your kidneys from producing urine completely.

options.C: Extra salt makes your body hold onto extra water, which pushes harder against your artery walls.
options.D: Salt causes your blood vessels to instantly expand and burst.

question: Which complication is most likely to show up months or years after an untreated septic abortion?

options.A: Acute kidney failure needing dialysis

options.C: A sudden hole in the womb with bowel exposure
options.D: Infertility caused by blocked fallopian tubes

explanation: Scar tissue from past infections can permanently block the fallopian tubes, making it hard to get pregnant later. Brilliant nursing knowledge!

question: Why should nurses treat every pregnancy as though complications could happen?

options.A: Routine delivery is considered a surgical emergency
options.B: Standard tests are rarely accurate during gestation
options.C: Complications can occur suddenly without prior warning
options.D: Most pregnant women develop chronic illnesses

explanation: Exactly! Even a smooth pregnancy can change quickly, so staying alert helps us catch issues early and save lives.

question: What is a major advantage of using lower individual drug doses in synergistic therapy?

options.A: It completely removes the need for nursing blood monitoring
options.B: It reduces the risk of toxic side effects for the patient
options.C: It allows patients to stop taking the drugs much sooner
options.D: It ensures the medication works instantly without absorption

explanation: Because the drugs boost each other, we can use smaller doses to get the job done, keeping the patient safer from harsh side effects.

question: Which group of workers faces the highest daily risk of exposure to bloodborne infections like HIV and Hepatitis B?

options.A: Healthcare workers
options.B: Textile factory weavers
options.C: Road construction workers
options.D: Office administrative staff

explanation: Because we frequently handle needles, sharps, and patient body fluids, healthcare personnel face a higher risk of bloodborne infections. Safety first!

question: How do nurses know how much pain a patient is actually feeling?

options.A: By checking changes in blood pressure
options.B: By measuring the exact amount of tissue damage
options.C: By trusting whatever the patient says it is
options.D: By looking for visible redness and swelling

explanation: You've got this! Pain is entirely personal. Since we can't see or touch it directly, the patient's own word is always our best and most reliable guide.

question: What is the specific name of the stress ulcer that forms in the stomach due to severe burn trauma?

options.A: Zollinger-Ellison ulcer
options.B: Cushing's ulcer
options.C: Peptic ulcer
options.D: Curling's ulcer

explanation: Think 'Curling' up from belly pain after a burn! It's a classic stress ulcer caused by low blood flow to the stomach early in shock.

question: Which of these nursing actions is a clear example of primary prevention focused on the host?

options.A: Screening blood samples for early signs of malaria
options.B: Providing physical therapy after a stroke
options.C: Treating severe complications in an intensive care unit
options.D: Administering routine childhood immunizations

explanation: Primary prevention stops disease before it even starts. Giving vaccines helps the body build a strong defense way ahead of any exposure.

question: What does a positively skewed distribution tell us about patient recovery times?

options.C: All patients recover in the exact same number of days

question: A client is quiet, avoids eye contact, and trembles slightly during your assessment. What might this suggest?

options.A: The client is ready for immediate hospital discharge
options.B: The client is hiding a contagious respiratory infection
options.C: The client may be experiencing significant emotional distress
options.D: The client has a normal blood pressure reading

question: What is the primary focus of pediatric palliative and hospice care at home?

options.A: Finding a cure for chronic genetic disorders
options.B: Enrolling the child in competitive school sports
options.C: Transferring the child back to the intensive care unit
options.D: Maximizing comfort, pain management, and family support

explanation: Well done! Palliative care is all about quality of life, easing pain, and bringing comfort to both the child and their loved ones. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T11#GNS324_U3_T11_h8)

question: Why is keeping the 'cold chain' so important when handling vaccines?

options.A: To make the injection feel more comfortable for the patient
options.B: To prevent the growth of harmful bacteria inside the glass vial
options.C: To ensure the chemical potency and effectiveness of the vaccine
options.D: To extend the manufacturer expiration date by several years

explanation: Brilliant! Heat can easily ruin the active ingredients in vaccines, rendering them useless if the cold chain breaks.

question: When is the right time for a nurse-midwife to practice hand hygiene in the labor ward?

options.A: Only at the beginning of the morning shift
options.B: Only after touching visible blood or amniotic fluid
options.C: Before and after every patient contact
options.D: After finishing all clinical duties for the day

explanation: Simple and non-negotiable: wash your hands or use sanitizer before and after every single patient touch to keep infections away.

question: What is the main feature of Type III FGM?

options.A: Removal of only the clitoral prepuce

question: A community health nurse notes that rural farmers frequently lose their harvests during the rainy season. What is the most likely underlying cause?

options.A: Excessive consumer preference for imported processed foods
options.B: Poor unpaved roads preventing trucks from reaching farms
options.C: Mandatory quarantine laws placed on all fresh vegetables
options.D: A sudden total ban on inter-state agricultural trade

question: What is a very common reason new mothers delay their first bowel movement after delivery?

options.B: Severe dehydration that dries out all body fluids
options.C: Complete lack of any urge to defecate for several weeks
options.D: Permanent paralysis of the colon caused by epidural anesthesia

explanation: Spot on. Soreness from stitches or swollen piles can make going to the toilet feel scary, so mums often hold back.

question: A community health nurse organizes a blood pressure screening camp at the local market square. What level of prevention is this?

options.A: Primary prevention

options.D: Secondary prevention

question: A client on combined oral contraceptive pills reports getting severe migraine headaches with visual changes (auras) lately. What should you do first?

options.A: Schedule her next routine appointment for five years later

options.C: Praise her for keeping her follow-up appointment on time

question: Which of these is an unhelpful thing to say to someone who is grieving?

options.A: Time heals all wounds.
options.B: I am here for you.
options.C: Would you like to talk about her?
options.D: It is okay to feel angry.

question: How do out-of-pocket payment systems negatively affect maternal health?

options.A: They cause families to delay seeking emergency medical treatment
options.B: They motivate nurses to work longer shifts without resting
options.C: They ensure that wealthy patients subsidize free community care
options.D: They improve the distribution of drugs in primary clinics

explanation: When patients have to pay cash immediately for every service, financial struggles often lead to dangerous delays in getting emergency care.

question: Why should a nurse apply pressure to an IV site immediately after withdrawing the catheter?

options.A: To ensure the plastic catheter tip remains intact inside the arm.
options.B: To push any remaining trapped air bubbles back up into the vein.
options.C: To stimulate rapid skin healing and eliminate scarring completely.
options.D: To stop bleeding and prevent hematoma formation at the site.

question: What is a baby or toddler's most important emotional need?

options.A: Secure attachment and safety
options.B: Financial independence
options.C: Meaningful career advancement
options.D: Peer group validation

question: A patient trapped under a heavy collapsed wall beam is experiencing which type of asphyxiation?

options.A: Environmental oxygen displacement

options.D: Cellular poisoning from toxins

question: What defense mechanism is happening when someone takes their frustration out on a safer, less threatening target?

options.A: Rationalization
options.B: Denial
options.C: Displacement
options.D: Projection

question: Why do researchers clean their data before running statistics?

question: Why does the pressure to have a baby boy often weigh so heavily on mothers in patriarchal societies?

question: What is the primary definition of homeostasis in the human body?

options.A: Stopping all electrical activity in the brain
options.B: Rapidly fluctuating blood pressure levels
options.C: Constantly increasing metabolic activity
options.D: Maintaining a stable internal environment

question: Which medical condition is much more common in pregnant teenagers compared to adult women?

question: Why do calming or sedating medications increase the risk of choking in older adults?

question: What is the main job of the pudendal nerve in the external genitalia?

options.A: Regulating local skin temperature

question: Why is drinking the water used to wash a deceased husband's body extremely dangerous for a widow?

options.A: Waterborne pathogens and infectious diseases from the corpse
options.B: Severe vitamin deficiencies due to lack of fresh fruits
options.C: Immediate permanent blindness from toxic chemicals
options.D: Chronic respiratory failure caused by cold temperatures

question: What is the main reason to encourage plenty of fluids for a patient with metabolic joint disease?

options.A: To dilute the blood so that red blood cells multiply faster
options.B: To prevent the stomach from absorbing purines from digested food
options.C: To keep the skin moist and prevent breakdown around the joints
options.D: To help the kidneys flush out excess metabolic waste products and prevent crystal formation

explanation: Drinking plenty of water helps the kidneys wash out uric acid before it has a chance to form painful crystals in the joints.

question: What is the primary reason for placing a patient with severe neutropenia on protective isolation?

options.A: To prevent them from leaving the ward before discharge
options.B: To keep their contagious blood disease away from others
options.C: To shield their fragile body from outside germs
options.D: To reduce the noise level around their hospital bed

question: What is the primary reason for encouraging high fluid intake after an intravenous pyelogram?

options.A: To prevent the patient from feeling hungry after fasting

options.C: To stimulate normal bowel movements following the procedure

question: Why does staring at a phone late at night make it hard for teenagers to sleep?

question: What is the term for non-living things like door handles or clothes that can pass germs from one person to another?

options.A: Vectors
options.B: Carriers

options.D: Reservoirs

question: What is a direct result of poor nutrition in an older adult going through rehabilitation?

options.A: Delayed wound healing and increased muscle weakness
options.B: Enhanced immune system function
options.C: Instant recovery from chronic stroke symptoms
options.D: Rapid muscle growth and increased strength

question: Why is it important to talk about birth control before the patient leaves the clinic?

options.C: To push the patient into long-term hormone use

question: Which of the following is an example of secondary data in a community assessment?

question: What role does regular feedback play in the philosophy of MBO?

question: Which of the following is an environmental hazard that increases fall risk in older adults?

options.A: Bright, glare-free overhead lighting

options.C: Properly fitted rubber-soled shoes
options.D: Sturdy handrails along the hallway

question: Why is keeping PAC patient information strictly confidential so important?

options.B: The Nursing Council requires permanent archiving of all case notes
options.C: It prevents insurance companies from raising premium rates
options.D: Hospital accreditation depends entirely on zero medical errors

question: What is the main reason for doing a pre-placement medical examination?

options.A: To test physical strength for office roles

options.C: To provide immediate treatment for interview injuries
options.D: To establish a baseline health status before a worker begins a job

question: A mother two weeks post-delivery feels hopeless, detached from her baby, and cannot sleep even when resting. What does this point to?

options.A: Expected physical fatigue
options.B: Postpartum thyroiditis
options.C: Normal postpartum blues
options.D: Postpartum depression

question: Why must nurses and doctors strictly avoid inserting fingers into the vagina (digital exam) when placenta praevia is suspected?

options.B: It introduces severe bacterial infection into the amniotic sac

question: What do we mean when we say a family caregiver is experiencing 'anticipatory grief'?

options.A: Grief experienced in anticipation of future losses and decline

options.C: Grief felt after the patient has already passed away

question: Which fetal position is required for a safe home delivery?

options.B: Breech presentation
options.C: Transverse lie
options.D: Oblique position

question: What is the main purpose of a community diagnosis?

options.C: To treat individual patients in a hospital ward
options.D: To assess the overall health status and needs of a population

explanation: A community diagnosis looks broadly at an entire group of people to find out their health problems, resources, and needs rather than focusing on just one patient. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T4#GNS124_U3_T4_h1)

question: What does 'deinfibulation' mean when managing FGM complications?

question: Why are nurses legally responsible for the medications they give to patients, even if a doctor prescribed them?

question: What protective action prevents food from entering the respiratory airway during a normal swallow?

options.C: The epiglottis folds down to cover the larynx
options.D: The hard palate drops down to seal the pharynx

question: How does successful disclosure directly support HIV treatment adherence?

options.B: It completely eliminates all possible side effects of the medication
options.C: Household members can offer practical reminders and emotional encouragement to take drugs
options.D: It forces the government to deliver medications directly to the patient's doorstep

explanation: Having a supportive person aware of the diagnosis helps patients take their daily medications consistently without hiding. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T8#GNS216_U6_T8_h4)

question: A 52-year-old woman comes to the clinic reporting hot flashes and irregular periods. What stage is she likely going through?

options.D: Menarche

question: How should a nurse respond when a patient insists their terminal test results belong to someone else?

options.A: Ignore the statement and change the hospital topic
options.B: Argue with the patient using hard medical facts
options.C: Agree with the patient that a mistake definitely occurred
options.D: Gently listen and avoid forcing immediate acceptance

question: Why is the patient medication profile essential in a unit dose setup?

question: How do robotic exoskeletons help patients recovering from a spinal injury or stroke?

question: What does a realistic healthcare plan take into account?

options.D: Current staffing levels and available budget

question: Why is a patient's Resting Metabolic Rate (RMR) usually a bit higher than their BMR?

options.C: It requires the patient to be completely unconscious

question: What does a therapeutic drug classification tell us about a medication?
